sections.title: The Erdős–Sós conjecture in dense graphs
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Erdős–Sós conjecture when the tree size is a fixed positive fraction of the host-graph order, and derive a Ramsey-number consequence.
sections.claimed_result: For every γ>0, sufficiently large n, and k≥γn, every n-vertex graph with more than (k−2)n/2 edges contains every k-vertex tree.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Simple n-vertex graphs, k-vertex trees, and the dense regime k linear in n.
sections.caveat: The abstract claims only the dense regime, so the general conjecture remains broader.

sections.title: Arithmetic Polyhedra
sections.abstract: The paper proves a conjecture that arithmetic hyperbolic reflection groups arising from combinatorial polyhedra are commensurable with those from three basic examples.
sections.claimed_result: All arithmetic ideal, right-angled hyperbolic polyhedra can be obtained by gluing copies of one of three seed polyhedra.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional hyperbolic reflection groups associated with combinatorial polyhedra, especially ideal right-angled hyperbolic polyhedra.
sections.caveat: The result concerns the arithmetic subclass and specified hyperbolic/polyhedral setting.

sections.title: Sophus Lie's problem on two-dimensional metrics with projective symmetries: completing the local classification
sections.abstract: The authors complete the local isometry classification of two-dimensional Riemannian and Lorentzian metrics with projective symmetry algebras of dimension at least two.
sections.claimed_result: A complete list of local normal forms is obtained for singular points where the projective Lie algebra action is non-regular.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Local two-dimensional pseudo-Riemannian metrics admitting projective symmetry algebras of dimension at least two; classification is up to isometry.
sections.caveat: Complete is local and up to isometry, not global.

sections.title: The weak-type (1,1) bound for the Hardy–Littlewood maximal function is O(√n log n)
sections.abstract: The authors improve the dimensional weak-type bound for the centered Euclidean Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator from O(n) to O(√n log n).
sections.claimed_result: The weak-type (1,1) estimate for centered maximal functions over Euclidean balls has dimensional dependence O(√n log n).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function, Euclidean balls, weak-type (1,1), dimension n.
sections.caveat: Optimality and removal of the logarithmic factor are not established here.

sections.title: Replica symmetry breaking at arbitrary depth
sections.abstract: In mixed even p-spin Ising spin glasses, the authors construct finite polynomial mixtures with exactly k-step replica symmetry breaking for every finite k.
sections.claimed_result: For each k≥1 there are finite polynomial mixtures whose Parisi measures are exactly k-RSB, with transitions between consecutive finite depths.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Mixed even p-spin Ising spin glasses at positive temperature and zero external field.
sections.caveat: The result concerns finite depths and the specified model class, not the full infinite-step phase.

sections.title: A Log-Free n^(1/5) Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
sections.abstract: The paper removes a subpolynomial/logarithmic loss from a recent lower bound in Chowla’s cosine problem.
sections.claimed_result: For every finite set S of positive integers, K(S)≥c|S|^(1/5) for an absolute c>0.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite sets of positive integers and the torus cosine sum in Chowla’s problem.
sections.caveat: The exponent 1/5 is established, but optimality is not claimed.

sections.title: Coleman Isomorphisms in Syntomic Cohomology and THH
sections.abstract: The paper generalizes Coleman’s isomorphism to several cohomology theories on proper regular p-adic formal schemes using motivically filtered THH and transfer maps.
sections.claimed_result: A generalized Coleman isomorphism is derived for cohomology theories evaluated on proper regular p-adic formal schemes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Proper regular p-adic formal schemes, required transfer structures, cyclotomic towers, and cited THH calculations.
sections.caveat: The abstract presents future Iwasawa-theory applications rather than proving them here.
